first.rationale: I currently intend a targeted, time-limited promotional pricing test for price-sensitive SMB prospects, given the competitor threat and the inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. I will verify the pricing record and the onboarding record because declining onboarding completion could confound results and pricing could increase low-quality or low-retention acquisition. The test should use qualification, retention, and margin guardrails rather than optimizing signups alone.

mid.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding simplification experiment. The verified record shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing this cycle: although it lifted qualified revenue 18%, 30-day retention fell 12%, creating unacceptable downstream value risk. Track activation, qualified revenue, time-to-value, and retention guardrails.

final2.rationale: Keep the committed onboarding simplification experiment for this cycle. It directly addresses the current completion and activation declines and has verified evidence of improved time-to-value and 30-day retention. Do not switch to broad promotional pricing in response to the deeper competitor cut: the verified discount test increased qualified revenue 18% but reduced 30-day retention 12%, undermining sustainable long-term revenue. Handle immediate SMB churn through non-experimental account communications and next-cycle testing of tightly targeted, retention-guarded pricing if needed.
